title: Hosting parity checklist and risk mitigation
body:
Goal: produce a concise, customer-facing checklist and mitigation playbook to ensure functional parity across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments for POC phase. This is deliberately practical — what we need to validate before committing to a recommended hosting path and what mitigations to have in place when parity cannot be achieved within the POC window.

Context: Customer wants low-latency chat with stricter data residency (EU) and an SLA target of 100ms median for short queries and acceptable p99 window of 700ms. They also expect infrequent on-prem access for sensitive back-office workflows. We need a POC that demonstrates: 1) correctness of outputs across model variants, 2) measurable latency & cost tradeoffs, 3) fallbacks and rollouts for capacity events, 4) compliance artifacts for data residency.

Checklist (functional parity categories):
- Model behavior parity:
  - Run identical prompt/eval suites against the hosted model, a dedicated cluster instance, and a private (VPC) deployment. Capture token-level diffs and top-level metric drift (BLEU/ROUGE-like proxies where applicable).
  - Acceptance criteria: per-prompt agreement >= 95% on classification/intent tasks; for generative tasks, human-eval delta <= 0.15 MOS on 50-sample blind eval set.
- Latency & throughput:
  - Baseline: 100k synthetic requests with the customer’s QPS distribution (spiky + diurnal). Measure p50/p90/p99 for each deployment mode, including cold-starts and warm steady-state.
  - Checkpoint: hosted must meet median requirement; dedicated should show predictable tail with reserved capacity; private may require local autoscaling policy tuning.
- Cost profile:
  - Calculate per-1M-token cost under observed QPS for each mode. Include egress, storage, and reserved GPU amortization for dedicated/private.
  - Flag if private cost delta > 40% vs hosted without clear compliance justification.
- Observability parity:
  - Ensure identical traces (request id propagation), token-level cost attribution, and model-version tagging exist in all modes.
  - Validate alerts and on-call runbooks trigger consistently for error-rate and latency SLO breaches.
- Security & compliance:
  - Data residency: confirm routing and storage behaviour (EU region pinning, KMS scope).
  - Audit logs: access events, model-change events, prompt retention policy must be demonstrably available in Private and Dedicated. Hosted: produce equivalent export and retention config.
- Feature parity (platform features):
  - Streaming responses, function/tool-calling interface, structured-output enforcement must behave identically (or documented differences) across all hosts.
  - Fallbacks: model-variant fallback (quantized vs float32) must be covered end-to-end with a test harness.

Risk matrix and mitigations (high-level):
- Risk: Quantization regression in dedicated/private causing unacceptable output quality.
  - Mitigation: maintain a small float32 canary pool; run A/B of quantized candidate on 10% of traffic in canary window; automated eval harness to detect regressions and rollback.
- Risk: Network egress and cold start tail in private deployments causing p99 spikes.
  - Mitigation: pre-warm KV caches during predictable windows; use burst capacity on dedicated for peak events; for private, add local request queue with priority eviction and circuit-breaker to degrade gracefully.
- Risk: Data residency leak via third-party telemetry or plugins.
  - Mitigation: denylist outbound hosts on private; optional telemetry redaction; require contract clause and architectural review for hosted telemetry.
- Risk: Unexpected cost delta for private due to low utilization of reserved capacity.
  - Mitigation: Coulple reserved capacity with burst-to-hosted policy; add autoscaler tuned to workload percentiles; set up cost alarms with daily burn-down.

POC validation plan (practical steps):
1) Test harness & canonical prompts:
   - Curate 120 prompts: 30 intents, 50 generative, 40 retrieval-augmented Qs. Include edge cases from customer transcripts.
   - Create automated scorer for intent accuracy, hallucination proxy (entity hallucination counts), latency per prompt.
2) Load generator & traffic shaping:
   - Replay historical traffic shape (if available) and synthetic spikes (4x baseline for 10m). Run 3 cycles per deployment mode.
3) Observability verification:
   - Instrumented tracing for every request, token billing tags, and model-version in traces. Export to a common metrics sink (Prometheus + Tempo) and run side-by-side dashboards.
4) Security & compliance checklist:
   - Demonstrate KMS key rotation, audit export, and region-locked storage. Capture screenshots and config snapshots as artifacts.
5) Runbook & rollbacks:
   - Document steps: scale-up dedicated pool, switch routing policy to hosted fallback, and TTLs for KV cache flush. Time-to-failover target: <120 seconds for traffic reroute.

Acceptance criteria (POC exit):
- All critical parity checks pass OR documented compensating controls exist and are validated.
- Observability parity: token-level cost attribution and model tracing present for each mode.
- SLA simulation: we can demonstrate reroute fallback preserves median latency while containing p99 tails within 2x of target.
- Security artifacts: audit logs and KMS proof-of-ownership for private/dedicated or exportable equivalents for hosted.

Customer-facing fallback strategy (recommended):
- Default-route: hosted for best cost/ops velocity during early rollout.
- Tiered fallback: dedicated reserved pool for baseline traffic (committed), hosted burst for spiky load, private for the regulated subset of traffic.
- Routing policy examples: route_by_policy = [region_priority, compliance_tag, latency_budget].

Open questions / tradeoffs to surface in the workshop:
- How strict is their definition of "EU-only"? Is encryption-in-transit + hosted EU region enough or do they require on-prem processing for some flows?
- Acceptance threshold for generative task MOS delta — is 0.15 acceptable or do product stakeholders require <0.1?
- Is there an existing SLA with legal implications that needs formalized uptime credits for Dedicated?
- Any hard constraints on telemetry sharing with hosted vendor? (some customers require zero telemetry export)

Next steps / immediate TODOs:
- Diego: produce the 120-prompt canonical suite (JIRA-1082). Due: 2025-01-21.
- Claire: spin up dedicated test cluster with quantized and float variants; enable tracing (CONF-2347). Due: 2025-01-23.
- Marcus: cost model template for 1M token scenarios across three hosting modes; include egress and KMS costs. Due: 2025-01-20.
- SRE: validate failover playbook with a dry-run on staging; record timeline. Due: 2025-01-28.

Notes to self: keep the POC scope tight — prioritize the 3 defenses that most frequently block deployment choices in previous deals: data residency proof, quantization/regression demonstration, and clear failover timings. Avoid trying to exhaustively reproduce internal enterprise audit processes during POC; deliver artifacts and a clear remediation plan instead.

Appendix (artifacts to attach after POC): screenshots of dashboards, config snippets for KMS and VPC peering, CSV of per-prompt diffs, cost worksheets, and a short executive summary slide (2 slides) for the customer executive review.

— End of working draft —

(If approved, convert remaining TODO items into a short customer-facing one-pager and a playbook with runbook checklists.)
